body.heading: Near is enough
paragraphs: A phone does not need to ring to distract you. Studies of attention suggest that even a silent phone sitting face-down nearby can take up some of your mental space, because part of you is quietly monitoring it.
That is why “I'll just ignore it” so often fails. Ignoring something within reach is work. Moving it out of reach is a one-time decision that keeps working for free.

body.heading: Make distance a routine
paragraphs: Choose one daily situation — homework, dinner, the first hour after waking — and put the phone in another room for it. Tell people who might need you where you will be, so the arrangement feels safe rather than dramatic.
Notice what the first few minutes feel like. The mild restlessness usually fades quickly, and what replaces it is often a surprising amount of getting things done.

takeaway: Distance beats willpower: move the phone, keep the focus.
